title: Estius: explicit faith of life-necessary articles and publicly taught dogmas
source_text: XXXII. Estius vero propositam quaestionem solvit his verbis: Sane dicendum videtur in primis unumquemque Christianum teneri ad distinctam seu explicitam fidem eorum articulorum, quorum distincta cognitio ad vitam recte instituendam est necessaria. Deinde ea fidei dogmata quae publice sunt satis obvia in Ecclesiastica doctrina, sive per praedicationem Pastorum, sive per frequentationem festorum, & usum ceremoniarum, explicite tenenda sunt omnibus iis qui justa ratione non impediuntur, quominus ea sic publice in Ecclesia proponi atque doceri videant, audiant & intelligant; eoque magis quo circa talia docenda major versatur Ecclesiae cura. Cujusmodi fere sunt quae diligentius inculcari solent contra graves haereses. In libr. 3. Sent. Dist. 25. q. 2.
pass_a_gloss: Estius solves the proposed question in these words: It seems that it must certainly be said, first, that every Christian is bound to distinct or explicit faith of those articles whose distinct cognition is necessary for rightly ordering life. Next, those dogmas of faith that are publicly sufficiently obvious in ecclesiastical doctrine, whether by the preaching of pastors or by the keeping of feasts and the use of ceremonies, are to be held explicitly by all who are not justly hindered from seeing, hearing, and understanding them as thus publicly proposed and taught in the Church; and all the more, the greater the Church care about teaching such things. Of this kind are roughly those that are more diligently inculcated against serious heresies (In libr. 3 Sent. Dist. 25, q. 2).
pass_b_english: Estius: every Christian owes distinct explicit faith to articles whose distinct cognition is needed to order life rightly.

Dogmas publicly obvious in church teaching — by preaching, feasts, ceremonies — must be held explicitly by all not justly hindered from hearing them, especially where the Church presses hard against grave heresies (Sent. 3 Dist. 25 q. 2).

choices.why: Estius expands explicit duty beyond bare Creed minimum.
rejected: only Creed articles ever need explicit faith
